decisions.reason: The citrus harvesting crate builds directly on the firm's core crate moulding and agricultural packaging know-how, so management can read its early market response and refine it in-house rather than abandon it after one year.

Foldable large containers are close to the firm's established automotive and industrial returnable packaging expertise, and the dedicated web page signals strategic commitment backed by in-house engineering.
A stackable plastic crate is a core-adjacent standard product where the firm's existing knowledge makes absorption and improvement straightforward and the resource burden low.
A medium-duty rackable pallet extends the firm's pallet engineering competence, so early results can be interpreted and fed back into design without unusual risk.
The spill-retention pallet is somewhat more niche, but it relies on existing pallet moulding skills, and its own web page indicates deliberate positioning worth continued learning.
A pallet with load retainers builds on the firm's pallet and handling-accessory expertise, has a dedicated presentation, and fits customer demand for secure reusable logistics.
